question_text: Draw an Instrumentation Amplifier (IA) configured for current sensing. What are its pros and cons?
answer_text:
Pros: Large input impedance allows measuring very small currents, and gain is easily changed with a single external resistor (R_g).
Cons: Common-mode voltage is limited to the supply voltage (V_CM <= V_s).
explanation_text: An Instrumentation Amplifier uses buffered inputs to achieve massive input impedance. It perfectly solves the PCB parasitic error issue by using a differential connection (measuring directly across the top and bottom of the shunt). However, because its internal op-amps are exposed to the input voltage, it cannot survive high common-mode voltages, restricting it primarily to low-side sensing (or very low-voltage high-side sensing).
